Good — that rules out the two most common culprits, and you've done a lot of the legwork already. Let's move to APN settings, which is the last device-level fix we can try.

**What APN settings are, briefly:** The APN (Access Point Name) is the set of technical instructions your phone uses to connect to our mobile network. If it's wrong or corrupted, your phone can have a perfectly fine, active SIM and still show "No Signal" — which matches exactly what you're seeing.

**Please check and do the following:**

1. Go to **Settings → Network & Internet (or Connections) → Mobile Network → Access Point Names (APN)**.
2. Look at what's listed and tell me the **APN name** and the **MMSC** field.
   - If anything looks obviously wrong — blank, or a name that isn't ours — stop and tell me.
   - If you're not sure what "correct" looks like, that's fine, just move to step 3.
3. Tap the **menu (⋮) → Reset to default** (on some phones it's "Reset APN to default").
4. **Reboot the phone** after resetting — the new settings won't take effect until you restart.

**After the reboot, check the status bar again.** If signal bars come back, please also turn **Mobile Data back ON** (Settings → Mobile Network → Mobile Data), since it was showing "Data Disabled" earlier.
